harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 9.5 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, and node3 (standbys), secured with a cluster-dedicated CA and mutual TLS requiring CA-issued client certs for replication. All three nodes were restarted one at a time and shown to fully recover, each with an independently verified changed boot identity.
actions_performed: Installed PostgreSQL 9.5 on node1, node2, node3
Created a dedicated cluster CA (ca.key/ca.crt) on node1 under /etc/postgresql-ca
Issued CA-signed server certs (CN/SAN = node IP+hostname) for all three nodes and a CA-signed client cert (CN=replicator) for the replication role
Distributed certs to node2/node3 over inter-node SSH using the cluster keypair; installed under postgres-owned /etc/postgresql/9.5/main/certs, key files chmod 600
Enabled ssl=on with CA/server cert/key on all nodes; set wal_level=hot_standby, max_wal_senders=10, wal_keep_segments=64, hot_standby=on, listen_addresses='*'
Created the replicator REPLICATION LOGIN role on node1
Restricted pg_hba.conf on node1 to hostssl replication for replicator from node2/node3 IPs using cert auth + clientcert=1, and reject plaintext (non-SSL) connections
Verified a connection without a client certificate is rejected and a connection with the CA-issued client cert over sslmode=verify-full succeeds
Bootstrapped node2 and node3 via pg_basebackup -R against node1 over TLS with the client cert, producing recovery.conf with sslmode=verify-full and cert paths
Started both standbys in recovery; confirmed pg_stat_replication shows both streaming with ssl=t and clientdn=/CN=replicator
Wrote and verified test data (repl_test table) replicated to both standbys
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline for all three nodes
Restarted node2, then node3, then node1 (primary last) one at a time via shutdown -r now, polling until reachable and proving changed boot_id each time

After each restart, verified postgresql auto-started (enabled service), standbys resumed recovery/streaming, and data was intact; after node1's restart, confirmed both replicas reconnected and a new write propagated to both

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication configured, node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys
evidence.summary: replicator role created on node1; pg_basebackup -R ran successfully against node1 for node2 and node3; both standbys started online,recovery; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both peers streaming

evidence.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a cluster-created CA
evidence.summary: CA generated on node1; server/client certs issued from it; ssl=on confirmed via SHOW ssl; recovery.conf shows sslmode=verify-full with CA-signed client cert paths; pg_stat_ssl on node1 shows ssl=t for both replication connections

evidence.requirement: Only accept replication connections from peers presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf restricts hostssl replication to cert auth + clientcert=1; a connection attempt without a client cert was rejected (FATAL: connection requires a valid client certificate); a connection with the CA-issued client cert succeeded and clientdn=/CN=replicator confirms the CA-issued identity was verified

evidence.requirement: Data actually replicates and remains consistent
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 (id=1) observed on both standbys; after all restarts, a second row (id=2, post-restart-check) inserted on node1 was confirmed present on both node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e881ab3c... and recovery state captured; shutdown -r now acknowledged (connection closed); immediate poll failed (connection refused) proving disconnect; boot_id changed to 46625cd4...; postgres online,recovery with data intact; node1 confirms node2 resumed streaming

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 847a859d... captured; restart acknowledged; poll shows connection refused then boot_id changed to a4cae457...; postgres online,recovery with data intact; node1 confirms both replicas streaming

evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f41e1f8a... and streaming replicas captured; restart acknowledged; poll shows connection refused then boot_id changed to 98b2b827...; postgres back online as writable primary with ssl=on; both replicas reconnected streaming and a new write propagated to both standbys

attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 9.5 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, and node3 (standbys), secured with a cluster-dedicated CA and mutual TLS requiring CA-issued client certs for replication. All three nodes were restarted one at a time and shown to fully recover, each with an independently verified changed boot identity.
